chunks: From Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, is not unjust to the servants in the distribution of reward.
And no deed performed by a doer for Him is lost with Him.

key_terms.الظَّالِم: Unjust / One who deprives of due right

ai.seo_question: What does Shia theology say about Allah's justice in rewarding deeds?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq’s (a) affirmation of divine justice (*‘Adl*), emphasizing that Allah’s accounting is precise and never neglects even the smallest good deed performed for His sake. This narration reinforces the Shia theological principle that reward is intrinsic to the act itself, ensuring no servant is wronged by the loss of their due recompense. It serves as a foundational proof for the reliability of divine record-keeping in the context of eschatological justice.
